title: Tech Note: Creating CSS Image Sprites files in 4D
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: CSS image sprites were a mainstream web-performance technique circa 2004-2015 for reducing HTTP requests, but the technique has become largely obsolete with HTTP/2 multiplexing (which removes most of the per-request overhead sprites were designed to avoid) and the rise of SVG icon systems and icon fonts; the note's underlying 4D picture-manipulation commands (COMBINE PICTURES, TRANSFORM PICTURE) remain functional, but the web technique itself is now a historical curiosity for most modern sites.
related_updates: HTTP/2 (and HTTP/3) multiplexing largely eliminated the request-overhead problem CSS sprites solved
SVG icons, icon fonts, and modern image formats (WebP/AVIF) replaced sprite sheets for most icon/graphic delivery
COMBINE PICTURES / TRANSFORM PICTURE remain valid 4D commands, just rarely used for this specific purpose now
